messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: Re: proposal for a Stat Computing section session at JSM 2014
parts:
Hi, Stan-developers.  See below.  Who'd like a trip to next year's Joint Statistical Meetings?
Andrew

On Aug 9, 2013, at 1:11 PM, Chris Paciorek wrote:

Ok, great.

As I email with the potential speakers should I correspond with you or is there a particular colleague you want to put me in touch with?

chris


On Thu, Aug 8, 2013 at 4:13 PM, Andrew Gelman <gel...@stat.columbia.edu> wrote:
Hi, Chris.  That sounds good to me.  I'm sure that one of my Stan colleagues would be interested in speaking at this.
A
On Aug 8, 2013, at 12:16 PM, Chris Paciorek wrote:

> Andrew,
>
> I'm trying to pull together an invited session proposal for next year's JSM highlighting recent work on general purpose software for hierarchical modeling. I'm getting in touch with folks from STAN, INLA, pyMC.  And our group is in the early development stages of developing a package called NIMBLE - Perry de Valpine, an ecologist/statistician is the PI for our project.
>
> The session could be fairly general with speakers highlighting recent cool stuff they have been doing, but it could also be a bit more focused with speakers talking about the software development challenges they've faced and solutions found during the process of building a general purpose tool.
>
> So if this sounds of interest, let me know if you or one of your STAN colleagues would be interested. And whether the more focused topic on software development challenges/solutions or the more general 'cool stuff' focus is more appealing to you. (Or if you have other thoughts within this broad area, let me know.)
>
> I'd need a tentative title by early September, but that would be about it for the moment.
>
> Chris
